articles.title: Bash Scripting: From Your First Script to Linux Automation
articles.excerpt: When I first started working with Linux, the terminal felt like a place where I typed mysterious commands and hoped they worked. I ran commands such as ls, cd, mkdir, and chmod. I literally copied com…
articles.body: When I first started working with Linux, the terminal felt like a place where I typed mysterious commands and hoped they worked. I ran commands such as ls , cd , mkdir , and chmod . I literally copied commands from documentation, fixed errors when something broke, and gradually began to understand what each command does. But eventually, you encounter a more interesting question: What if you could combine these commands into a program that makes decisions and performs tasks automatically? That is where Bash scripting comes in. In this article, we will move from the fundamentals of Bash to practical concepts such as variables, conditions, command-line arguments, file permissions, environment variables, executable commands, and scheduled tasks.
articles.author: Juma Evans

articles.title: Learn Term Gates by Building a Tiny Definition Card
articles.excerpt: Last Tuesday a campus library in Halifax felt like a waiting room for dying batteries. Mine hit 11 percent just as a chat tab handed me three slick sentences about precision and recall. They sounded s…
articles.body: Last Tuesday a campus library in Halifax felt like a waiting room for dying batteries. Mine hit 11 percent just as a chat tab handed me three slick sentences about precision and recall. They sounded sharp enough to paste into my notes. I closed the lid anyway. Thursday the tab was gone, and a classmate asked for the counterexample. All I had was a polished paragraph, with no fixture, no command, and no expected fail. Have you ever tried to rebuild a lab from the feeling that it looked right? This is the card I should have saved before the battery died. { "id" : "hidden-stem" , "term" : "precision" , "sentence" : "Precisionism is a style, not a metric." , "expect" : false } A substring check would accept it, because "precision" is hiding inside "Precisionism".
articles.author: Alex Chen

articles.title: This Framework Compiles Java Straight to CUDA: Can It Really Match llama.cpp?
articles.excerpt: Every Java team that touches local AI knows the same story. You build a clean Spring Boot or Quarkus service, then someone says "we need inference on our own GPU," and suddenly your tidy JVM stack has…
articles.body: Every Java team that touches local AI knows the same story. You build a clean Spring Boot or Quarkus service, then someone says "we need inference on our own GPU," and suddenly your tidy JVM stack has a Python sidecar bolted to the side. PyTorch, a CUDA toolkit, a second Dockerfile, a second set of CVEs, and a REST hop between the two halves of your own application. On October 8, a project started making the rounds on r/LocalLLaMA with a claim that attacks exactly that pain: a Java framework that compiles Java bytecode down to CUDA and cuTile, running LLM inference on NVIDIA GPUs at a claimed 90% of llama.cpp performance. No C++ code, no Python process, no sidecar. The project is jitLLM, built by the TornadoVM team at the University of Manchester with Red Hat as a collaboration partner.

articles.title: 105K Impressions, 659 Clicks: A Search Console Teardown
articles.excerpt: Over the last 92 days (2026-07-07 to 2026-10-06), a tax calculator site I have been working on pulled 104,826 Google impressions and 659 clicks across 182 pages that earned at least one impression. A…
articles.body: Over the last 92 days (2026-07-07 to 2026-10-06), a tax calculator site I have been working on pulled 104,826 Google impressions and 659 clicks across 182 pages that earned at least one impression . A 0.63% click-through rate. If you saw only that number you would close the tab and move on. But those 659 clicks and those 104,826 impressions are two completely different stories stacked on top of each other, and the split between them is the whole lesson. This is a straight Search Console export, no smoothing, no "estimated" numbers. The headline numbers Metric Value Period 2026-07-07 to 2026-10-06 (92 days) Clicks 659 Impressions 104,826 CTR 0.63% Pages with impressions 182 Total pages in sitemap 326 Less than 60% of the site ever showed up in the results at all.

articles.title: Building a FANUC CNC Data Collection and OEE System Without Replacing Your Machines
articles.excerpt: Picture a machine shop with a dozen FANUC CNC turning centers and machining centers. At the end of each shift, the production supervisor walks around with a clipboard, writing down cycle counts from e…
articles.body: Picture a machine shop with a dozen FANUC CNC turning centers and machining centers. At the end of each shift, the production supervisor walks around with a clipboard, writing down cycle counts from each machine's display. Someone else checks alarm logs to figure out why Machine 7 was down for two hours. By the time the data gets into a spreadsheet, it's already yesterday's news. The machines themselves can tell you what's happening — FANUC CNC systems expose operational data through their communication interfaces. The challenge isn't the machines; it's getting that data out, making sense of it, and putting it somewhere people can actually use it.

articles.title: NASA Demonstrates Next-Generation Heat Shield Technologies
articles.excerpt: NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24th cargo resupply missi…
articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) A KREPE-3 capsule floats inside the Northrup Grumman Cygnus XL 24 cargo spacecraft on October 7. Inside the capsule is a 3-D printed heat shield designed by researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. NASA NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24 th cargo resupply mission for NASA undocked from the International Space Station, it carried a fleet of 12 small, experimental capsules designed to test the next generation of thermal protection materials that could serve as the foundation for future heat shields.

articles.title: Cosmic House of Mirrors
articles.excerpt: Galaxies warp and multiply as if in a house of mirrors in this image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Sept. 29, 2026. The brilliant golden galaxies seen here are part of a galaxy clu…
articles.body: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Furtak, S. Fujimoto Galaxies warp and multiply as if in a house of mirrors in this image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Sept. 29, 2026. The brilliant golden galaxies seen here are part of a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies bunched together on one side of the image, however, are not actually part of the cluster, but rather galaxies much farther away whose light has been bent and magnified by gravitational lensing. This phenomenon occurs when the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Learn more about this galaxy cluster. Image credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, L. Furtak, S. Fujimoto

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 9… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Stickney Crater Explanation: Stickney Crater, the largest crater on the martian moon Phobos, is named for Chloe Angeline Stickney Hall, mathematician and wife of astronomer Asaph Hall. Asaph Hall discovered both the Red Planet’s moons in 1877. Over 9 kilometers across, Stickney is nearly half the diameter of Phobos itself, so large that the impact that blasted out the crater likely came close to shattering the tiny moon.
